en.p: For a real number $t$ with $t>\dfrac{1}{2}\ln 2$, let $f(t)$ be the distance between the two distinct points where the curve $y=\ln(1+e^{2x}-e^{-2t})$ meets the line $y=x+t$. When $f'(\ln 2)=\dfrac{q}{p}\sqrt{2}$, find the value of $p+q$. (Here $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
